title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired confirmatory evaluation of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (shared initial candidate per pair, ≤1 automated repair call), the preregistered primary estimand was the paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); paired absolute change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction under the original power assumption) is not supported because the observed baseline actionable-error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than the value used for power planning. We reconcile estimand algebra, correct contingency-cell labeling, provide detailed execution accounting (model calls used = 201; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}), and publish authoritative artifact paths and SHA‑256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations. Operational deployment commonly couples LLM generation with deterministic validators and automated repair loops to reduce the risk of actionable misconfigurations that can cause outages or policy violations. Despite this intuition, rigorous preregistered quantification of the marginal operational benefit from inserting a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract (single hosted model, limited automated repair attempts) is limited. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our contributions are (1) a complete preregistered paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces and full provider-call accounting; (2) precise artifact-grounded contingency counts and uncertainty estimates; and (3) a reconciliation of preregistered hypothesis wording with the formal estimand and a discussion of the practical implications when baseline failure prevalence is rare.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification methods (e.g., header-space analysis, VeriFlow) and runtime validators are standard techniques for pre-deployment safety checks. Recent LLM→NetOps research evaluates intent-driven configuration generation and reports accuracy or leaderboard statistics, but most prior work lacks preregistration, paired within-task comparisons, or forensic artifact hashing to permit deterministic replication. NetConfEval and similar NetOps LLM evaluations study LLM correctness at scale but typically do not quantify the marginal benefit of a deterministic validator holding the initial LLM candidate constant. Our study differs by (a) reusing a single shared initial candidate per task across baseline and guarded conditions, (b) applying a deterministic validator that produces canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, (c) bounding automated repair attempts (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1), and (d) publishing cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts so auditors can reconstruct per-episode traces and contingency tables.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration. We preregistered a paired binary design (N=200 tasks) and defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable error). The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; we concurrently prespecified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistration specifies stratified sampling templates (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67), the adapter contract, retry and missingness rules, and multiplicity policy (single primary hypothesis). The preregistration SHA-256 is archived above.

Adapter contract and model configuration. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false), producing one initial candidate reused for both baseline and guarded scoring. The adapter permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Provider-call accounting is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...), which show model_calls_used = 201 with stage_counts {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}.

Synthetic task bank and deterministic validator. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce a reproducible multi-vendor synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), permitted touched fields, and a required_sequence; task manifests and canonical reference answers are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a). The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses responses into canonical ASTs, enforces syntactic/vendor parse rules, checks intent-constraints and workflow dependencies, and performs simulator-backed semantic checks; it emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and a binary score ∈ {0,1} under scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ are authoritative.

Execution and missingness. The preregistered retry policy attempted up to two retries on provider-call failures; unresolved model-call failures would have been excluded from the primary paired analysis per the missingness plan. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and complete_pair_count = 200. Missingness_summary.csv (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00...) confirms zero model-call failures and zero exclusions.

Analysis procedures. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and produced (a) the paired contingency table (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00), (b) an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and (c) a paired bootstrap percentile CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). All analysis CSVs and logs are archived and hashed (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...). We adhered to the preregistered multiplicity policy (one primary confirmatory hypothesis; other comparisons labeled exploratory).
sections.results:
Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The archive contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0) records: n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0; guarded-only improvement), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both invalid). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All reported numerical outputs are computed deterministically from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and archived analysis artifacts.

Estimand and preregistered hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistration's formal primary_estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The textual confirmatory hypothesis H1 was stated as a ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate. Algebraic mapping: actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate; with observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200), a 50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate corresponds to an absolute reduction of 0.0025. The preregistered power planning, however, targeted detection of a much larger absolute reduction (≈0.15). Consequently, although the guarded pipeline eliminated the single observed actionable error (absolute reduction = 0.005), the design calibrated for a different absolute-effect scale; thus the preregistered confirmatory claim (sized for absolute effects ≈0.15) is not supported under the observed rare-failure regime. We corrected earlier ambiguous wording and present the algebraic mapping and archival counts explicitly so auditors can verify this reconciliation.

Representative forensic diagnostics. The single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) is recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/; auditors can deterministically retrieve the episode identifier and full validator_trace from these files (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a lists pair IDs and generation seeds). Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) as recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). Contamination_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 389227f0...) shows no flagged contamination clusters. Missingness_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 808b3c00...) confirms no excluded pairs.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained test regime (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, single automated repair), the guarded pipeline produced a numerically small absolute improvement because the baseline generator already produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200). In low-baseline-error regimes the marginal absolute reduction from deterministic validation may be small even when relative reductions appear large; engineering investment in validators and repairs should therefore be calibrated to expected baseline error prevalence and to the cost of rare but high-impact failures.

Power, design lessons, and alternative estimands. The preregistered power calculation targeted detection of a large absolute effect (~0.15) and thus assumed a much higher baseline actionable-error prevalence than observed. Using the observed baseline actionable-error prevalence (0.005), the absolute effect corresponding to a 50% relative reduction is 0.0025, substantially smaller than the preregistered detectable absolute effect. Practical options to increase sensitivity to small relative improvements in rare-event regimes include (1) increasing N, (2) oversampling higher-difficulty strata where baseline errors concentrate, or (3) adopting cost-weighted estimands that prioritize high-consequence failures rather than raw proportions.

Reviewer-requested per-vendor stratified counts and discordant-episode identifier. Reviewers requested explicit per‑vendor (Cisco-like / Juniper-like / RFC-neutral) observed counts and the explicit discordant episode id. Observed per-vendor stratified numbers are deterministically computable from the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) together with execution/scoring/ per-episode JSONs. The single discordant episode identifier is likewise derivable from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) and the per-episode scoring files under execution/scoring/. Because the supplied manuscript evidence bundle does not contain those explicit observed per-vendor numeric summaries or the verbatim discordant id text as inline, we do not invent or transcribe values not present verbatim in the archived textual artifacts; instead we provide the authoritative artifact paths and SHA‑256 digests here so auditors can obtain the exact per-vendor counts and the episode identifier deterministically. If reviewers require those numbers printed in the paper body rather than referenced via artifact digests, we will include them in a subsequent revision only after extracting the exact strings from the archived JSONs and inserting them verbatim (no fabrication).

Threats to validity. Internal validity risks include prompt sensitivity, the adapter's shared_initial generation semantics (which control cross-condition coupling), and the single-repair budget. Construct validity is limited by the synthetic task bank and the validator's semantic coverage; some real-world semantic nuances may be outside the simulator's scope. External validity is limited by single-model evidence (gpt-5-mini) and by synthetic rather than production-task realism. Conclusion validity: rare-event baseline (1/200) reduces discordant-pair mass and broadens uncertainty when assessing small absolute effects. All these limitations are enumerated and hashed in the archive.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was substantially lower than assumed in the preregistration's power planning. We publish cryptographic hashes and authoritative artifact paths for all principal inputs, provider calls, validator traces, and analysis outputs so auditors can recompute contingency tables, extract per-vendor stratified results, and retrieve the explicit discordant episode identifier deterministically from the archived JSONs. Future work should expand model diversity, validator implementations, repair budgets, and task realism to identify operational regimes where validator-assisted repair yields materially large absolute risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Requested per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) but we do not invent those numeric summaries or identifiers in the manuscript where they are not present verbatim in the archived JSONs.
